text.content: Weekly marketing report: 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25
Week 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-25: spend 6434.72 USD against 6362.61 the week before, 95 sign-ups (GA4 key events) against 107, so a cost per sign-up of 67.73 against 59.46 USD.
KPIs
Key events: 95 vs 107 (-11.2%)
Cost per key event: 67.73 USD vs 59.46 USD (+13.9%)
Organic clicks: 1477 vs 1405 (+5.1%)
Platform conversions this week (each platform's own count, not added up): Google Ads 65.6, Meta Ads 57, LinkedIn Ads 7, TikTok Ads 8.
What moved

Online Booking Search (Google Ads): impressions 12267 -> 9327 (-24.0%), clicks 555 -> 408 (-26.5%), conversions 28.1 -> 21.0 (-25.3%). The pull shows fewer clicks for the same spend because each click cost 41% more; why the cost per click rose is not visible in this data: auction insights or impression share (not pulled for a dashboard) would show whether a competitor or a bid change caused it.
Retargeting, site visitors 30 days (Meta Ads): conversions 35 -> 27 (-22.9%). Clicks held, so the change is in conversions per click; cause not visible in this data.
Budget and plan
October pacing after 27 of 31 days: Google Ads 1.03 (on pace); Meta Ads 1.55 (overspending); LinkedIn Ads 1.01 (on pace); TikTok Ads 0.97 (on pace).

Plan vs live: Budget differs, Online Booking Search: live daily budget 350.00 against 300.00 in the plan (+16.7%); Missing, Competitor Search: planned live from 2026-10-14; no live campaign with this name spent between 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-27; Not in plan, Retargeting, site visitors 30 days: spent 1861.26 between 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-27 and has no plan row. LinkedIn Ads and TikTok Ads are pulled at account level, so their campaigns are not matched against the plan.
Next week
Meta Ads is at pace 1.55: at this rate October ends near 9319.47 USD against a budget of 6000.00. Lower its daily budgets or agree a higher October budget.
Online Booking Search: check auction insights and the bid strategy's change history for 2026-10-19 onward, when its cost per click stepped up.
Plan: launch Competitor Search or take it out of the plan, set Online Booking Search's daily budget back to the plan or update the plan, and add the Meta retargeting campaign to the plan.
Dashboard (tabs Dashboard, Daily, Weekly, Campaigns and Budget): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<SPREADSHEET_ID>/edit

looker_studio_dashboard.honesty_line: Looker Studio has no public API that builds pages or charts, so the layout comes as build steps. The data, calculated fields and blend are ready to use, and a Linking API URL opens a report already connected to the staged tab.

spec.reader_and_decision: The founder and the marketing lead, Monday: move budget between the four ad platforms or not.
questions: What did we spend and how many sign-ups did we get last week, against the week before?
Which platform and campaign bring sign-ups at the lowest cost?
What does one sign-up cost across all paid spend?

kpis.name: Platform conversions
kpis.formula: SUM(Conversions), shown per platform, never added across platforms

spec.refresh: LS_Daily is a snapshot: it gains days when this skill is asked to append them. Looker Studio re-reads the sheet every 15 minutes (its default).
not_included: ROAS: no conversion values are set on any of the four ad accounts (Conversion value is 0 on every row)
Search Console: connected through Google's own connector by the user, not staged

source_plan.route: LS_Daily (staged), so all paid spend sits in one table
Google's own connector, blended with LS_Daily on Date

staged_tab.name: LS_Daily
staged_tab.reporting_currency_column: not needed: every account bills in USD

data_checks: Complete days: Google Ads, Meta Ads and LinkedIn Ads returned all 14 days; TikTok Ads returned 12, and 2026-10-18 and 2026-10-19 came back as an empty list (no delivery), not a gap.
One currency: all four accounts report in USD.
Reporting day: Google Ads, Meta and TikTok days are in America/New_York; the LinkedIn call returns days without a time zone, noted in the spec.
Totals match: the 82 staged rows add up to 12797.33 USD, the sum of the four platform totals below.

ratio_of_sums_check.why_it_matters: A stored daily CPA column averaged in Looker Studio gives 71.54; the true cost per conversion for the period is 78.75. The average also drops the 2 days with spend and no conversions, where a daily CPA can't be computed.

calculated_fields.formula: Spend with the chart's Percent of total comparison calculation

blend.field: Blended cost per sign-up = SUM(Spend) / SUM(sign_up)
blend.why_not_platform_conversions: The four platforms claim 283.9 conversions together while GA4 recorded 202 sign-ups from every channel. Platforms credit some of the same sign-ups, so the KPI divides by GA4's count.

build_sheet: Open https://datastudio.google.com/reporting/create?ds.connector=googleSheets&ds.spreadsheetId=<SPREADSHEET_ID>&ds.worksheetId=<LS_DAILY_SHEET_ID> while signed in with an account that can open the spreadsheet.
Data source: Date as Date (YYYYMMDD); Spend and Conversion value as Currency (USD); add the 5 calculated fields above; data freshness 15 minutes.
Add GA4 and Search Console with Google's own connectors, then blend LS_Daily with GA4 on Date (full outer) and add Blended cost per sign-up to the blend.

Overview page: scorecards for Spend, Sign-ups, Blended cost per sign-up and CPA with previous period comparison; a time series of Spend and Sign-ups; a table by Platform with Spend, Conversions, CTR and CPA.
Campaigns page: a table by Platform and Campaign with Spend, Clicks, Conversions, Conversion rate and CPA, sorted by Spend.
Website and search page: GA4 sessions and sign-ups by day, Search Console clicks by day.
Controls on every page: a date range control with comparison to the previous period, drop-down filters for Platform and Account, and a 'Data through' scorecard of MAX(Date) from LS_Daily.
Sharing: data source credentials set to the owner's, report shared as view only, scheduled email delivery every Monday at 08:00 to the two readers.

review_of_current_report.check: Rate stored as a column and averaged
review_of_current_report.what_is_wrong: The TikTok CTR scorecard averages the export's daily CTR column.
review_of_current_report.why_it_misleads: It shows 0.74%; clicks over impressions for the same rows is 0.63%.
review_of_current_report.fix: Delete the CTR column from the export and add CTR = SUM(Clicks) / SUM(Impressions) on the data source.

review_of_current_report.check: Platform conversions added into one total
review_of_current_report.what_is_wrong: 'Total conversions' adds Google Ads and TikTok conversions (131.9 + 5).
review_of_current_report.why_it_misleads: Both platforms can claim the same sign-up, so the total counts some sign-ups twice.
review_of_current_report.fix: Show conversions per platform, and use GA4 sign-ups for the one total.

review_of_current_report.check: Blend on Date with an inner join
review_of_current_report.what_is_wrong: The Spend by day chart joins Google Ads and the TikTok export with an inner join.
review_of_current_report.why_it_misleads: Only the 6 days that have a TikTok row survive: 8 of the 14 days in the range drop out, with 3292.11 USD of the 5728.73 USD Google Ads spend.
review_of_current_report.fix: Use a full outer join on Date, or move both platforms into LS_Daily and drop the blend.

review_of_current_report.check: Staged source with no 'data through' date
review_of_current_report.what_is_wrong: The TikTok export ends on 2026-10-17 while the report shows 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-25.
review_of_current_report.why_it_misleads: The last 8 days show no TikTok activity, which reads as a pause rather than a missing paste.
review_of_current_report.fix: Replace the hand-pasted export with LS_Daily and add a MAX(Date) scorecard.

review_of_current_report.check: Scorecard with no period or comparison
review_of_current_report.what_is_wrong: 'Total conversions' shows no period label and no comparison.
review_of_current_report.why_it_misleads: The reader can't tell which dates the number covers or whether it went up.
review_of_current_report.fix: Turn on the previous period comparison and label the date range in the scorecard's title.

review_of_current_report.check: A filter that applies to one side of a blend
review_of_current_report.what_is_wrong: not visible in what was shared
